hook: Three flats of 1907 on the Dupont Street site where the First Colored Baptist Church built its first church in 1854.

parcel.planning_name: SITE OF FIRST COLORED BAPTIST CHURCH; TH
parcel.note: Planning's historic resource survey names this parcel "SITE OF FIRST COLORED BAPTIST CHURCH; TH" — the dataset truncates the field at 40 characters. Grant Avenue was formerly Dupont Street. The building standing here now went up in 1907, after the church had left the site.

assessment.note: Every roll year from 2018 through 2025 records this parcel at a 0.1 ownership share, so the assessed figures above are a partial interest, not the whole parcel. They are not charted on this page for that reason.

historical_record.description: The congregation left this site for a building at Bush and Powell Streets, which the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed.
The congregation took the name Third Baptist Church, as the third Baptist communion founded in the city and to be an inclusive church without a racial designation.

The First Colored Baptist Church of San Francisco moved into its first church building, on Dupont Street between Greenwich and Filbert. The State of California's historical landmark registration application for the congregation gives the address as 1642–44 Grant Avenue.
Nine Black Christians gathered to begin the religious and social-cultural activities of the congregation, on Dupont — now Grant Avenue — between Greenwich and Filbert.

narrative.lead: Grant Avenue was formerly Dupont Street. The flats standing here now went up after the congregation had left the site.

unknowns: The Argonaut has the congregation beginning its activities here in 1852; SF Planning's landmark designation report has it forming that year at a private residence on Kearny Street and moving into this building in 1854.
The Argonaut dates the congregation's employment of its first pastor, the Reverend Charles Satchell, to 1854; the designation report dates it to 1856.
